## In 60 seconds

Impedance localization turns every catheter electrode into a position sensor. Pairs of skin patches drive small
high-frequency currents through the chest, separated by frequency or time, and the system reads the potential each
pair makes at each electrode. If the field were uniform, position would be potential divided by field. It is not: the
potential of a patch pair is $k(1/|\mathbf r - \mathbf a| - 1/|\mathbf r - \mathbf b|)$, and along its axis
$2kx/(d^2 - x^2)$, so a uniform-field map stretches positions toward the patches by $x^2/(d^2 - x^2)$. Real chests
add more distortion where conductivity changes, because the field rises in proportion to the conductivity ratio.
**Field scaling** uses electrodes of known spacing: each pair satisfies $\ell^2 = \Delta\boldsymbol\phi^\top M
\Delta\boldsymbol\phi$, which is linear in the local metric $M$. Precision is voltage noise divided by field strength.

## From the field

- **Any electrode can be located.** Regular catheter electrodes, used as sensors for a high-frequency transthoracic
  field applied through skin electrodes, gave positions that were highly linear with the true ones (correlation
  0.996–0.999). Electrogram recordings were unaffected [@wittkampf1999].
- **Scaling is the weak point.** The same work reported localization accuracy better than 2 mm, with an additional
  scaling error of 8% to 14% [@wittkampf1999].
- **Distances vary from chamber to chamber.** A 54-mm electrode span on a decapolar catheter measured 101% ± 15%,
  95% ± 10% and 97% ± 8% of its true length in the right atrium, right ventricle and left ventricle
  [@wittkampf1999b].

## Derivations

**Symbols used throughout.** $I$ patch current; $\sigma$ conductivity; $k = I/(4\pi\sigma)$; $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$
patch positions; $\phi$ potential; $d$ patch half-separation; $x$ position along the axis; $E_0$ field at the center;
$\boldsymbol\phi$ the vector of three pairs' potentials; $J$ the local Jacobian $\partial\boldsymbol\phi/\partial\mathbf
x$; $M$ the local metric; $\ell$ known electrode spacing; $\sigma_{\text{ref}}$, $\sigma_{\text{local}}$ conductivities
of a reference and a local region; $\delta\phi$ voltage noise.

### A patch pair

In a homogeneous medium, current $I$ entering at $\mathbf a$ and leaving at $\mathbf b$ makes the potential (m02):

$$
\phi(\mathbf r) = k\left(\frac{1}{\lvert\mathbf r - \mathbf a\rvert} - \frac{1}{\lvert\mathbf r - \mathbf b\rvert}\right), \qquad k = \frac{I}{4\pi\sigma}
$$ {#eq-m17-pair}

It is harmonic between the patches and odd about the plane midway between them. Real chests are bounded and
inhomogeneous, which changes the numbers but not the shape of the argument.

### The nonlinearity

On the axis between patches at $\pm d$:

$$
\phi(x) = \frac{2kx}{d^2 - x^2}, \qquad E_0 = \frac{2k}{d^2}, \qquad \frac{\phi(x)/E_0 - x}{x} = \frac{x^2}{d^2 - x^2} \approx \frac{x^2}{d^2}
$$ {#eq-m17-axis}

A system that assumes a uniform field reports positions too far out, increasingly so toward the patches: with $d$ =
200 mm, by 1.0% at 20 mm and 6.7% at 50 mm (lab part A).

### A linear map

Three orthogonal pairs, separated by frequency, give three potentials per electrode. The simplest map divides each by
its central field:

$$
\hat x_i = \frac{\phi_i(\mathbf r)}{E_0}, \qquad i = 1, 2, 3
$$ {#eq-m17-linear}

It is exact only at the center. Over a cube of half-width 0.2$d$ the RMS error was 1.8 mm, and over 0.4$d$ it was
13.9 mm (lab part B).

::: {.demo #m17-d1 badge="exact"}
```{=html}
<div id="m17-d1-root" class="demo-root" data-demo="m17-d1"></div>
<script type="module" src="../demos/m17-d1-axis.js"></script>
```

**Assumptions**

- Model: point patches in an unbounded homogeneous medium, @eq-m17-axis, mapped by @eq-m17-linear. Tested against
  `epml.impedance`.
- Parameters: patch separation and probe position are illustrative choices.
- What it ignores: the torso's boundary, lungs and other inhomogeneities, patch size and respiration.
:::

**Key takeaways**

- A uniform-field map stretches positions toward the patches.
- The error grows as the square of the distance from the center relative to the patch separation.

### Field scaling from known spacing

Catheter electrodes have known spacings. Locally $\Delta\boldsymbol\phi = J\Delta\mathbf x$, so $\Delta\mathbf x =
J^{-1}\Delta\boldsymbol\phi$ and:

$$
\ell^2 = \lvert\Delta\mathbf x\rvert^2 = \Delta\boldsymbol\phi^\top M\,\Delta\boldsymbol\phi, \qquad M = (JJ^\top)^{-1}
$$ {#eq-m17-metric}

Each electrode pair of known spacing gives one equation, linear in the six independent entries of the symmetric $M$.
Pairs in at least six independent orientations near one place determine it. In the lab, twelve orientations of a 4-mm
bipole fix $M$, and a 10-mm pair that the uniform-field map reported as 13.0 mm is measured as 10.0 mm (lab part C).
This is one way to formalize field scaling; products do not publish their methods in this form.

::: {.demo #m17-d2 badge="exact"}
```{=html}
<div id="m17-d2-root" class="demo-root" data-demo="m17-d2"></div>
<script type="module" src="../demos/m17-d2-grid.js"></script>
```

**Assumptions**

- Model: two orthogonal point-patch pairs, @eq-m17-pair, in an unbounded homogeneous medium; the grid lies in their
  plane and is mapped by @eq-m17-linear. Tested against `epml.impedance`.
- Parameters: grid size and patch separation are illustrative choices.
- What it ignores: the third pair's influence off the plane, the torso's boundary, inhomogeneity and any correction.
:::

### Inhomogeneity

Across an interface between regions of different conductivity, normal current density is continuous (m02,
[eq-m02-interface](m02-volume-conduction.qmd#eq-m02-interface)), so the field, and with it the apparent distance,
scales with the conductivity ratio:

$$
\frac{E_{\text{local}}}{E_{\text{ref}}} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{ref}}}{\sigma_{\text{local}}}
$$ {#eq-m17-interface}

A 10-mm layer at half the reference conductivity appears 20 mm thick (lab part D). Lungs, the blood pool and the
myocardium all differ in conductivity, which is why impedance geometry needs scaling, and why hybrid systems anchor it
with magnetic sensors (m18).

### Precision

Voltage noise becomes position noise through the field strength:

$$
\delta x = \frac{\delta\phi}{\lvert E\rvert}, \qquad \lvert E_0\rvert = \frac{2k}{d^2}
$$ {#eq-m17-precision}

Closer patches or more current give a stronger field and less position noise, but closer patches also make the
nonlinearity worse (@eq-m17-axis). With $d$ = 150 mm the stretch at 60 mm is 19%; with 300 mm it is 4.2% (lab part E).

**Key takeaways**

- Known electrode spacings calibrate the local field.
- Conductivity changes stretch apparent distance.

## Clinical correlate

::: {.callout-note title="Pending clinical review"}
This section describes published findings only. It is not guidance for patient care, and it has
not yet been reviewed by an EP physician.
:::

**Where this shows up in EP.** Impedance localization lets a mapping system show every electrode of every catheter,
not just those with magnetic sensors [@wittkampf1999]. Its geometry depends on scaling: early work reported a scaling
error of 8% to 14% [@wittkampf1999], and measured inter-electrode distances varied by chamber [@wittkampf1999b].
Respiration and changes in the chest's impedance during a procedure can shift positions over time (m19).

**What the evidence is.** Two clinical validation studies from the same group [@wittkampf1999; @wittkampf1999b].

**What a reader should ask:**

- **Were positions scaled, and with what?** (@eq-m17-metric)
- **How far from the center of the field was the measurement?** (@eq-m17-axis)
- **Did the catheter cross regions of different conductivity?** (@eq-m17-interface)

## How experts think

When judging impedance-based geometry, ask:

1. **Where is the region of interest relative to the patches?** (@eq-m17-axis)
2. **What map turns potentials into positions?** (@eq-m17-linear)
3. **How was it scaled, and from which electrode spacings?** (@eq-m17-metric)
4. **Which conductivity boundaries lie nearby?** (@eq-m17-interface)
5. **What is the position noise?** (@eq-m17-precision)

One sentence to keep: **potential is not position until the field is known, and electrodes of known spacing tell you
the field.**

## Cheat sheet

| Quantity | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Patch pair (@eq-m17-pair) | $k(1/\lvert\mathbf r - \mathbf a\rvert - 1/\lvert\mathbf r - \mathbf b\rvert)$, $k = I/(4\pi\sigma)$ |
| Axis (@eq-m17-axis) | $2kx/(d^2 - x^2)$; $E_0 = 2k/d^2$; stretch $x^2/(d^2 - x^2)$ |
| Linear map (@eq-m17-linear) | $\hat x_i = \phi_i/E_0$ |
| Field scaling (@eq-m17-metric) | $\ell^2 = \Delta\boldsymbol\phi^\top M\Delta\boldsymbol\phi$, $M = (JJ^\top)^{-1}$ |
| Interface (@eq-m17-interface) | $E_{\text{local}}/E_{\text{ref}} = \sigma_{\text{ref}}/\sigma_{\text{local}}$ |
| Precision (@eq-m17-precision) | $\delta x = \delta\phi/\lvert E\rvert$ |

**Values used in this module**

| Value | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Correlation 0.996–0.999; accuracy better than 2 mm; scaling error 8–14% | @wittkampf1999 |
| 54-mm span measured at 101% ± 15%, 95% ± 10%, 97% ± 8% | @wittkampf1999b |
| Patch separations, grid sizes, conductivity ratios, noise | illustrative |
| Stretch, map errors, field-scaled distances | our own code |

## Interview questions

Try each question before you open its model answer. In a real interview, say which assumptions you
are making.

**Q1. How does impedance localization turn an electrode into a position sensor?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Skin patch pairs drive high-frequency currents; the electrode's potential from each pair, separated by frequency,
depends on its position (@eq-m17-pair) [@wittkampf1999].

</details>

**Q2. Why are the currents at high frequency?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

To separate them from the electrograms and from each other by frequency, and so the electrograms are unaffected
[@wittkampf1999].

</details>

**Q3. Derive the nonlinearity along a patch pair's axis.**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

$\phi = k(1/(d - x) - 1/(d + x)) = 2kx/(d^2 - x^2)$; dividing by $E_0 = 2k/d^2$ overshoots by $x^2/(d^2 -
x^2)$ (@eq-m17-axis).

</details>

**Q4. Where is a uniform-field map most accurate?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Near the center between the patches (@eq-m17-linear).

</details>

**Q5. How can known electrode spacing calibrate the field?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Each pair satisfies $\ell^2 = \Delta\boldsymbol\phi^\top M\Delta\boldsymbol\phi$, linear in the metric $M$; pairs in at
least six orientations determine it (@eq-m17-metric).

</details>

**Q6. Why does one straight catheter in one orientation not fix the metric?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

All its pairs point the same way, giving one direction's scale only; the other five entries of $M$ need other
orientations (@eq-m17-metric).

</details>

**Q7. Why do lungs distort impedance geometry?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Normal current is continuous across conductivity boundaries, so the field and apparent distances change with the
conductivity ratio (@eq-m17-interface).

</details>

**Q8. What sets position noise?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Voltage noise divided by field strength (@eq-m17-precision).

</details>

**Q9. Trade-off in moving patches closer together?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

A stronger field and less noise, but more nonlinearity across the heart (@eq-m17-axis, @eq-m17-precision).

</details>

**Q10. Impedance against magnetic localization: one strength and one weakness each.**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Impedance locates every electrode but needs scaling and can drift; magnetic localization measures distance directly but
needs sensor coils and is disturbed by conductors (m16).

</details>

**Q11. What did early validation report for scaling?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

An additional scaling error of 8% to 14% on top of better than 2 mm accuracy [@wittkampf1999].

</details>

**Q12. A map's chamber looks 10% too large. What would you check?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Model answer</summary>

Whether field scaling was applied and from which catheter, where the chamber sits relative to the patches, and whether
the patches or the chest impedance changed (@eq-m17-axis, @eq-m17-metric).

</details>

## Self-check

Short checks you can do in your head. Open each answer after you have tried it.

**S1. Patches at ±200 mm. Stretch of a uniform-field map at 40 mm?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

$1600/(40000 - 1600) \approx$ 4.2% (@eq-m17-axis).

</details>

**S2. Patch separation doubles. Central field?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

One quarter (@eq-m17-axis).

</details>

**S3. How many independent pair orientations to determine the local metric?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

Six (@eq-m17-metric).

</details>

**S4. A layer has one third the reference conductivity. Apparent thickness of a 5 mm layer?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

15 mm (@eq-m17-interface).

</details>

**S5. Voltage noise doubles. Position noise?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

Doubles (@eq-m17-precision).

</details>

**S6. A uniform-field map reports a 10 mm pair as 13 mm. Is the region nearer the patches or the center?**

<details class="model-answer">
<summary>Answer</summary>

Nearer the patches, where the field is stronger (@eq-m17-axis).

</details>

## Literature figures

These figures are worth looking at alongside this module. We link to them instead of copying them:
some licenses do not allow reuse here, and others we could not confirm. Each entry says what to
look for and where this module explains it.

- **Measured against true electrode positions.** Wittkampf and colleagues' linearity results in three chambers
  [@wittkampf1999]. This module: the nonlinearity and field scaling.
- **Distances during ablation procedures.** The same group's measured inter-electrode distances by chamber and
  procedure [@wittkampf1999b]. This module: field scaling.
